feedback.goal: Upgrade the tau-style demo into a statistical claim: per-batch cluster identity so iterative loops re-cluster cleanly, and a multi-seed pass@k driver with a paired comparison gate.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Cluster identity binds the failure fingerprint to the run batch; records carry batch_id; dal cluster run filters by batch.
The driver repeats each task N times with unique run/receipt ids and writes a per-batch summary with per-task mean, pass@1, checkpoint-union, and overall mean/variance.
--compare pairs two summaries and passes only when the task set matches, no overall or per-task mean regresses, and every receipt is digest-valid and binds its recorded state digest.
Repository-wide gate passes with the change.

outcome.summary: Cluster identity now includes the batch (additive batch_id on cluster records, --batch filter in the CLI), and the e2e driver gained --attempts/--compare with receipt-bound pass@k summaries. Focused tests and the full gate pass.

what_worked: Fingerprint+batch cluster ids keep iterative loops re-clusterable without CLUSTER_ID_CONFLICT.
The compare gate validates every receipt against its recorded state digest (BRANCH_RECEIPT_MISMATCH fails the gate).

uncertainty.statement: The live multi-seed G0/G1 demonstration has not completed yet; the statistical claim itself is not yet produced.
uncertainty.resolution: Run both legs once the per-skill approval decisions exist, then judge G1 against G0 with --compare.
